To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the glucuronic acid, the glucuronyltransferase activity and the excretion of estroges with urine were decreased in patients with benign and especially with malignant tumors of breast, but this decrease did not reach the level of significance.

the activity of glucuronide transferase is reduced in patients with breast cancer, but this is not a specific feature of this tumor, since it is also found in patients with benign breast tumors, and in patients with breast fibrocystic disease, as well as in healthy individuals.

the decrease in the activity glucuronyl transferase and increase in percentage of free (unconjugated) estrogen is noted in patients with malignant mammary gland tumor, and the analogous results are obtained in patients with breast tumors, although these are statistically insignificant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of glucuronylation in the metabolism of estrogens in the mammary gland.
the role of the glucuronic acid in the formation of estrogens conjugates and in the metabolism of the latter.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no evidence that glucuronyl transferase activity or serum glucuronic acid levels are useful in the diagnosis or prognosis of breast cancer.
the activity of glucuronosyltransferase is not a specific marker for breast cancer, and the decrease of its activity in the blood and the urine may be a sign of relative hyperestrogennemia.
the decrease in the activity glucuronyl transferase is a result of relative hyperestrogensia in normal total excretions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the decrease in the activity and the increase in the percentage free estrogens in the blood of the patients with breast tumors, the increase in the excretion of estriol and the decrease in the excretion 17-KS in the urine, and the decrease in glucuronyl transferase in the serum of these patients are all evidence of the presence of relative hyperestrogens in patients.

the decrease in the activity glucuronyl-transferase in the blood serum of patients with benign and, in particular, with malignant tumors of mammary gland is the result of the relative hyperestrogenism, which is a consequence of the increased activity of aromatase.
